judgments.question: Give the four Association task strengths, side-I/II task limits, worker requirements when repeating a task before a break, and whether other players workers matter.

requested_parts.part: Task strengths are reputation two, partner three, university four and conservation five
observed_clause_quotes: Association tasks are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4 and conservation project work

summary_support.quote: - **Increase reputation (strength 2):** increase your zoo's reputation by **2**, taking any track bonuses you reach.

- **Gain partner zoo (strength 3):** take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty partner-zoo space of your map (take any printed bonus immediately). All your partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum 4 total; the third (or fourth) requires the upgraded Association action. If every zoo currently on the board is one you already have, or you cannot place it, you cannot perform this task. Each partner zoo reduces the cost of Animal cards from its continent by 3 money per continent icon, provides 1 icon of that continent (usable for card effects and conservation projects), and some Animal cards require one.

- **Gain university (strength 4):** take a university from the Association board onto the lowest available university space and **immediately resolve both its covered-space bonus (if any) and the university tile’s own reputation award (if any)**. You cannot take a duplicate university. Universities grant reputation and research icons and are the only way to increase your hand limit to 5.

- **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). **The Base Conservation Projects below the board never move and are never replenished**, even when fully supported.

summary_support.quote: - **Side I:** Perform **exactly one association task**. You need at least 1 active association worker: place it on the chosen task on the Association board. summary_support.quote: - **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

summary_support.quote: - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. summary_support.quote: **Upgrading Action cards.** All Action cards start on side I. When you receive a card upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II (it stays in its slot); its improved action is available **from your next action**, while it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. The current action keeps the strength and kind set at its start; an upgrade gained during it does not add side-II capabilities to it. There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. One of them allows you to choose an alternative — so you cannot upgrade all of your Action cards.

Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). judgments.question: Which displayed symbols count as icons in your zoo, which do not, do effects count their own card and repeated icons, and which text wins if a card conflicts with a general rule?

requested_parts.part: Upper-right Animal and Sponsor icons count
observed_clause_quotes: Zoo icons include upper-right icons on Animal/Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements.

summary_support.quote: Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

summary_support.quote: 3. **Fill an empty enclosure:** any animal except Petting Zoo animals can go on its own into an empty **standard enclosure** of at least the required size (hexagon number); flip the enclosure to its occupied side. Count distinct adjacent hexes: multiple edges touching the same water hex still count as only one, and a larger water area counts only the hexes actually adjacent. Petting Zoo animals go **only** in the Petting Zoo. All reptiles and some birds can instead go in their special enclosure (Reptile House / Large Bird Aviary) — such cards show both enclosure requirements and you choose (water/rock requirements apply to the special enclosure too). To house an animal in a special enclosure, mark the number of spaces shown on the card with player tokens from your supply; if not enough free spaces remain in the special enclosure, it cannot go there. Special enclosures are never flipped.

Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.
